issues.failure_explanation: In the tanh case the theorem minimizes g_tanh(ζ) = ⟨ζ, artanh(ζ)⟩ over feasible non-reparametrized ζ, but the correct objective (per Corollary cor:TrigonometricRegularization and the proof sketch) is g_tanh(ρ_rp(ζ)) = g_tanh(tanh(ζ)) = ⟨tanh(ζ), ζ⟩, i.e. g_tanh evaluated at the reparametrized variable. These are different functions of ζ. Moreover g_tanh(ζ) = ⟨ζ, artanh(ζ)⟩ is undefined for |ζ_i| ≥ 1 so the stated minimization is not even well-defined on all feasible ζ. The sinh case of the same theorem correctly applies g_sinh to ρ_rp(ζ), confirming the intended pattern.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace g_tanh(ζ) with g_tanh(ρ_rp(ζ)) = g_tanh(tanh(ζ)) in the minimization of the tanh case, matching the sinh-case pattern and the statement of Corollary cor:TrigonometricRegularization.
issues.overall_effect: The showcase theorem's tanh case advertises the wrong implicit regularizer. A reader following the theorem would compute ⟨ζ, artanh(ζ)⟩ instead of the correct ⟨ζ, tanh(ζ)⟩ (equivalently ⟨ζ̃, artanh(ζ̃)⟩ on the reparametrized domain). The correct result is available in Corollary cor:TrigonometricRegularization.
issues.title: Wrong objective function in tanh case of showcase theorem
issues.why_classification: A single local correction (changing the argument of g_tanh) restores consistency with the corollary and the proof. All substantive claims and guarantees survive; no new lemma, construction, or argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This clearly contradicts the local uniqueness of the trajectory $\wprod$ since on $(\t_\star-\varepsilon,\t_\star)$ both the original trajectory $\gamma_1(\t) = \widetilde w_i(\t)$ and the constant trajectory $\gamma_2(\t) = \widetilde w_i(\t_\star)$ are solutions for \eqref{eq:with_sigmaout_PreVersion}.
By choosing $\bm\mu = \0$, we automatically satisfy dual feasibility and complementary slackness.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers local Lipschitz continuity of the vector field from continuity. This is false: for ρ_rp(z)=z^{2/p} with p∈(1,2) the w̃-coordinate vector field contains the factor h′(w̃)^{-1} ∝ w̃^{2-p} with 2-p∈(0,1), which is Hölder but not Lipschitz at w̃=0. Picard–Lindelöf uniqueness therefore fails and solutions of ẋ = -cx^α with α∈(0,1) reach x=0 in finite time. Part (i) is false. Part (ii) is also false: after boundary-hitting, some coordinates freeze while the identity g = w̃′⊙h′ used in Lemma theorem:vector_general breaks down (h′(0)^{-1}=0 while g_i≠0), so h(w̃_∞)−h(w̃_0) need not lie in range(Aᵀ) and the proof incorrectly sets the active-boundary KKT multiplier μ=0. A concrete counterexample with N=3, M=2, A=[[1,1,0],[0,1,1]], y=(1,1), ρ_rp(z)=z^{4/3}, w̃_0=(ε,2,2) shows the trajectory converges to (0,1,0) whereas the Bregman projection from w̃_0 onto {ζ̃≥0 : Aζ̃=y} = {(t,1-t,t)} is at (1/5,4/5,1/5).

failure_location.quote: Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:with_sigmaout_PreVersion} is a continuous function of $\wprod$ on $\R^\N$ by Assumptions \ref{as:A1}-\ref{as:A3}, it is locally Lipschitz continuous at any point.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (a) restrict Theorem theorem:vector_IRERM and its polynomial dependents to reparametrizations for which the w̃-coordinate vector field is locally Lipschitz on D_rp (excluding polynomial ρ_rp with p∈(1,2)), or (b) develop a new argument handling boundary-hitting trajectories, e.g. allowing nonzero KKT multipliers at active boundary constraints and proving the required sign condition on the post-freezing contribution ∫g_i dτ. Option (a) loses the regime p∈(1,2); option (b) requires new proof architecture.
issues.overall_effect: The implicit bias characterization—the paper's central claim—can fail for polynomial reparametrizations with p∈(1,2): the gradient-flow limit need not minimize the advertised Bregman divergence over the feasible set. Lemma lem:decay and Theorem thm:Convergence are unproven for reparametrizations allowing boundary-hitting trajectories, cascading to the polynomial convergence corollary and the showcase polynomial theorem. Results for sinh and tanh reparametrizations are not affected because the vector field is locally Lipschitz at the boundary in those cases.
issues.title: Implicit bias theorem is false: trajectory can hit boundary in finite time
issues.why_classification: The implicit bias characterization— the main result—is false as stated. Option (a) excludes the advertised regime p∈(1,2) (the interpolation between ℓ₁ and ℓ₂ regularization). Option (b) needs essentially new proof architecture (boundary-hitting analysis with nonzero KKT multipliers). No supported resolution preserves the full advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To use Theorem \ref{theorem:vector_IRERM}, we have to verify Assumption \ref{as:A2} for $\wDomain = \wDomainRP = \R_{\ge 0}^\N$.
Assume that there exists $\z_0 \in \R_{>0}^\N$ with $\A\z_0 = \y$ and set $\sigmainn(\w_0) = \alpha \bo$, for $\alpha > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:PolynomialRegularization (and likewise cor:PolynomialRegularizationNonAsymptotic, cor:TrigonometricRegularization, and cor:TrigonometricRegularizationNonAsymptotic) assume only that the reparametrized limit w̃_∞ exists. Their proofs apply Theorem theorem:vector_IRERM, which additionally requires L(w_∞)=0 (equivalently LossM(w̃_∞)=0). This hypothesis is never verified in the corollary statements or proofs. Without it w̃_∞ need not be a feasible point of the claimed minimization; e.g. if y ∉ range(A) the feasible set {ζ̃ : LossM(ζ̃)=0} is empty and the displayed equality is false. The showcase theorems in the introduction do include this hypothesis (as existence of ζ_0 with Aζ_0 = y), confirming it is intended but omitted from the detailed corollaries.

failure_location.quote: Define $\wprod_0 = \sigmainn(\w_0) = \alpha \bo$, for $\alpha > 0$, and assume that $\wprod_{\infty,\alpha} := \lim_{\t \to \infty} \sigmainn(\w(\t))$ exists for any $\alpha$ sufficiently small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis L(w_∞)=0 (or equivalently Assumption as:B2: existence of ζ̃_0 ∈ int(D_rp) with Aζ̃_0 = y) to the statements of cor:PolynomialRegularization, cor:PolynomialRegularizationNonAsymptotic, cor:TrigonometricRegularization, and cor:TrigonometricRegularizationNonAsymptotic.
issues.overall_effect: The implicit-bias corollaries for both polynomial and trigonometric reparametrizations are unproven without the hypothesis that the flow converges to a global minimizer of the loss. The showcase theorems include this hypothesis so their statements are unaffected.
issues.title: Missing hypothesis L(w_∞)=0 in implicit-bias corollaries
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis (already present in the showcase theorems) to the corollary statements is a short, routine repair that preserves every substantive claim and guarantee. No new lemma, construction, or argument is needed.
